solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Exasperated request, left hand raised, to return and suspend missing father

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the three pieces before it are read backwards

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left
H is the abbreviation for hand
something raised is up

indicators.note: a word missing something has lost it, so the letters for father come out

parts.note: to freeze a payment or activity is to suspend it
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Someone raises a hand in irritation, begging a returning father to stay his hand.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across entry 'raised' simply means up, not upward reading; the reversal comes from 'to return', which turns round everything before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Puh-leeze is a mocking drawn-out version of please, the exasperated plea of someone who has had enough.

clue.text: Illustration accompanying books, extremely elaborate, with darker edges

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, a flower whose petals have darker edges; the definition describes it adjectivally

parts.note: pic is short for picture, an illustration
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the following word, its very first and very last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of elaborate

explanation.surface: An illustrated book with elaborate dark borders around its pages.
explanation.walkthrough: PIC + OT + EE gives PICOTEE. OT, the Old Testament, is a crossword staple for books.
explanation.definitionFit: A picotee is a carnation or similar bloom whose pale petals are bordered with a contrasting deeper colour.

clue.text: One talking up high, not allowing husband to be lower?

definitions.text: not allowing husband to be lower?

parts.note: one who hypes something, talking it up
gamy describes meat that is high, strong-smelling from hanging

explanation.surface: A social climber with lofty ambitions refuses to marry beneath her.
explanation.walkthrough: HYPER + GAMY. 'High' looks like part of the social-climbing picture, but it is the smell of hung game.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypergamy is marrying a partner of higher social rank, which rules out taking a spouse from a lower station.

clue.text: Young migrants meeting flow of social assistance after reversal of original direction

indicators.note: reversing a compass direction swaps it for its opposite point, so one letter is exchanged for another

parts.note: welfare is state help for those in need
the opening letter of welfare happens to be a compass direction, west

explanation.surface: Young people arriving in a country encounter the benefits system.
explanation.walkthrough: The W at the start of WELFARE is West; reversing that direction gives East, E, so EELFARE.
explanation.definitionFit: An eelfare is the passage of young eels upstream against the current of a river, or the brood itself.

clue.text: Sea monster god's energy is providing twice, back to back

indicators.note: back to back means the second copy faces the opposite way, so it is written backwards
saying one thing is another here means it is replaced by it

parts.note: Zeus is the king of the Greek gods
E is the symbol for energy
if means providing, as in 'providing it rains', written twice

explanation.surface: A sea monster belonging to a god keeps supplying energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' works as an equals sign: the god's energy becomes the doubled word, with the second copy facing backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ziffius is an old name, found in Spenser, for a fearsome whale-like creature of the ocean.

clue.text: Music player with glower cut short drum

indicators.note: something cut short has lost its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a DJ, disc jockey, plays music
read as glow-er, something that glows, like a coal in a dying fire

explanation.surface: A scowling musician has his drum confiscated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glower' is not a scowl but a thing that glows, read as glow-er.
explanation.definitionFit: A djembe is a goblet-shaped hand drum from West Africa played with bare hands.

clue.text: Assisted in East End hotel: lifted top drawer and pocketed order?

indicators.note: London's East End is home of the Cockney accent, which famously swallows an initial aspirate

parts.note: did help is an emphatic way of saying assisted
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: in a down entry something lifted is raised up the column, so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, top drawer; the figure 1 is written as the letter I

explanation.surface: A Cockney hotel worker helps out, then pinches something from the top drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney says 'did 'elp' for did help. A1 means first-class, and the 1 doubles as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Didelphia was an old name for the marsupials, the order of mammals whose females carry young in a pouch.

clue.text: Send out guards to put a stop to flashing

indicators.note: to guard something is to stand around it, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: to emit is to send out
to can something, as in 'can it!', is to stop it

explanation.surface: Dispatching security guards to stop someone exposing himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flashing' suggests indecent exposure but means sparkling; 'can it' is slang for stop it.
explanation.definitionFit: Emicant is a rare word for sparkling or darting out light, from Latin for springing forth.

clue.text: Gift turning up the month after it's due, a crushing blow

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means flipping to read upward, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: this gift is due in January, so the month after is February
to fan is to blow air
taken as written

explanation.surface: A belated present arrives a month late and is a bitter disappointment.
explanation.walkthrough: FEB turned up is BEF, then FAN and A. The Befana gift is given at Epiphany, in January.
explanation.definitionFit: In Italy a befana is a present given at Epiphany, named after the old woman of folklore who brings it.

clue.text: Busy year resulted in journalist getting published without restrictions

parts.note: busy is old slang for a police officer
Y is the abbreviation for year
a crash that left him lame resulted in it
ED, editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A busy year ends with a reporter's work going out uncensored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busy' looks like an adjective but is slang for a police officer. COP + Y + LEFT + ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Copyleft is a licensing scheme letting anyone use, change and share a work freely, the reverse of copyright.

clue.text: News, oddly absent, didn't flow

indicators.note: with the letters in odd positions absent, only the second, fourth and so on remain

parts.note: the even letters of didnt flow, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Some news is missing because the reports stopped coming through.
explanation.definitionFit: Info is a casual shortening of information, the facts or reports that make up news.

clue.text: Clay's farewell boxing blunder is a flipping breather!

indicators.note: boxing means putting in a box, so the farewell surrounds what follows

parts.note: ta-ta is a casual goodbye
to err is to blunder

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the two short words before it read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a gill is what a fish breathes with

explanation.surface: Boxer Cassius Clay says goodbye, and fighting is an exhausting business.
explanation.walkthrough: Clay suggests the boxer later called Muhammad Ali, but it is earth; 'flipping' looks like a mild curse but turns round only 'is a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Terra sigillata is a fine red earthenware, the clay used for glossy Roman tableware.

clue.text: Film's about university in US provinces

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's alien film, plus the S of the possessive
Yale is an American Ivy League university

explanation.surface: A film is set around an American university out in the provinces.
explanation.walkthrough: ET is the crossword's favourite film.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyalets were the large administrative divisions of the Ottoman Empire, each governed by a pasha.

clue.text: Slimline drinks in vending machine, to cut out sweetener

indicators.note: drinking something in takes it inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: slimline means thin

indicators.note: to cut something out is to remove it, so that short word goes

parts.note: an automat is a coin-operated vending machine or the cafeteria built from them
taken as written, then removed

explanation.surface: Diet drinks from a vending machine, to cut down on sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: An automat is chiefly American: a coin-operated food machine, or a cafeteria made of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Thaumatin is an intensely sweet protein from a West African fruit, used as a low-calorie sugar substitute.

clue.text: Producer of tack for local religious feast repulsed temple

parts.note: Whit is Whitsun, the Christian festival of Pentecost

indicators.note: something repulsed is driven back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia

explanation.surface: A local saddler is turned away from a temple at a church festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For local' marks a dialect word. Tack here is a horse's harness and saddlery, not a small nail.
explanation.definitionFit: Whittaw is a northern English dialect name for a saddler or harness-maker, who makes horse tack.

clue.text: Neat turns somehow producing effect outside the mind

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are put together any which way

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Tidy turns somehow have an effect on the outside world.
explanation.definitionFit: Transeunt is a philosophical term for action that passes beyond the agent to produce results in the external world.

clue.text: Welsh swimmer, close to buoy, wading out

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged
the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of buoy
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A Welsh swimmer heads for a buoy and wades out of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests a Welsh athlete; it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The gwyniad is a whitefish found only in Bala Lake in Wales, so a swimmer native there.

clue.text: Docker down under working mostly when fair

indicators.note: working means in operation and on the move, so the letters are rearranged
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: taken as written, losing its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Australian docker works only when the weather is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: Down under is Australia, and Australian slang shortens words with -ie.
explanation.definitionFit: Wharfie is the Australian and New Zealand slang term for a wharf labourer, a man who loads ships.

clue.text: Drag artiste's bottom hidden, fully exposed bust

indicators.note: something hidden is out of sight, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: nude means completely uncovered

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of artiste, which is removed
to nick is to arrest, as is to bust

explanation.surface: A drag queen's bare backside is covered up but her bust is on full display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drag' is not a drag act but a bore; 'bottom' and 'bust' are not body parts either.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudnick is a Yiddish-derived word for a pest or bore, someone who is tiresome company.

clue.text: Feline with claw pared gets cross

indicators.note: pared means trimmed at the end, so the final letter comes off

parts.note: a cat is a feline
a talon is a claw

explanation.surface: A cat gets angry after having its claws clipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' is not angry but a hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattalo is a hybrid bred from domestic cattle and the American bison, so a crossbreed.

clue.text: State constant, universal principle in broadcast coming up

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

indicators.note: in a down entry coming up means reading from the bottom upward, so backwards
one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
the Tao is the underlying principle of the universe in Chinese philosophy

explanation.surface: A nation's unchanging founding principle emerges in a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tao, the Way, comes from Chinese philosophy; c is the physicist's speed of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Croatia is a sovereign country on the Adriatic, and a state is an independent nation.

clue.text: Mum finds out from me after one has dropped plants

indicators.note: after places the word that follows behind the one before it in the answer

parts.note: she finds out because someone tells her
the telling comes from me, so the speaker is I
ma is a familiar word for mother
surface padding: the one moves down, below the telling, in this down entry

explanation.surface: Mother discovers from me that someone has planted some flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: The scene is 'I tell Ma'; the one, I, drops below the telling in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Tellima, fringecups, is a genus of North American woodland perennials grown in shady gardens.

clue.text: Tiny cox frantically releasing a lot of corrosive stuff

definitions.text: releasing a lot of corrosive stuff

indicators.note: frantically means in a wild disordered rush, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A small Cox apple oozes acidic juice, a Cox being a variety of English apple.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxyntic describes stomach cells or glands that secrete hydrochloric acid in quantity.

clue.text: Spotted piece of game pie initially, then finally, stopping a past slimming operation

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so these letters go inside the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
to go by is to go past
a domino is a spotted tile from the game of dominoes

indicators.note: initially points to the start of the word, its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of pie
last means finally, as in 'at last'

explanation.surface: A dieter eats a piece of game pie, then stops eating to lose weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted piece of game' leans on game pie but is a tile from dominoes; to go by is to go past.
explanation.definitionFit: Abdominoplasty is cosmetic surgery removing excess skin and fat from the belly, a tummy tuck.

clue.text: Quietly force approval from Elysée Palace, ditching old, sceptical reaction

indicators.note: ditching means getting rid of, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
F is the symbol for force
oui is French for yes, and the Elysée Palace is the French president's residence
O is the abbreviation for old, the letter dropped

explanation.surface: Quiet pressure to win French presidential approval meets a dismissive response.
explanation.walkthrough: P + F + OUI without O. 'Force' is the physics symbol F, not pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Pfui is an exclamation of contempt or disbelief, like pooh or phooey.

clue.text: Slack outfit from the Right is OTT, awkwardly embracing America First

indicators.note: reading from the right means right to left, so the whole thing goes backwards
to embrace is to hold in your arms, so the scrambled letters surround the next piece
awkwardly means clumsily put together, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; OTT is over the top
the US is America
1st, with the figure 1 written as the letter I

explanation.surface: A sloppy right-wing outfit, over the top and clumsily wrapped in America First slogans.
explanation.walkthrough: TIOST around US1ST gives TIUSISTOST, which read backwards is TSOTSI SUIT. 'Right' looks political but is the direction of reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsotsi suit is a flashy South African township style of dress with tight-ankled baggy trousers, slacks.

clue.text: Sky no longer used source for broadcast by similar group

indicators.note: broadcast speech is heard rather than read, so what matters is how the words sound

parts.note: a well is a source of water
kin are a family group, people alike by blood

explanation.surface: Sky TV drops a channel that used to be broadcast by a similar network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sky' suggests the British broadcaster; it is the heavens. 'No longer used' marks the word as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Welkin is an archaic and poetic word for the vault of heaven, the firmament above.

clue.text: Half-fall of Briton in time accounts for fencing manoeuvre

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
AC is the abbreviation for account, here two of them

indicators.note: half means only part of the word survives, its first half

parts.note: what Americans call fall, a Briton calls autumn

explanation.surface: Half of a Briton's fall in time accounts for a fencing move.
explanation.walkthrough: Fall is the American word for the season; a Briton says autumn. A/c is the bank abbreviation for account.
explanation.definitionFit: Tac-au-tac is a fencing term for a parry followed immediately by a riposte, a rapid exchange of blows.
